headline: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called for stronger AI regulation, including a narrow government power to block deployment of unsafe AI.
score_reason: Direct on-record interview with the head of a leading AI lab on regulation; fresh and read in full.
importance_line: It affects lawmakers weighing AI rules and workers worried about jobs, but it is a company chief's proposal and nothing has been enacted.
summary: ABC News reports, in an exclusive interview that its Philadelphia station 6abc carries, that Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei is proposing stronger regulation, including giving the government the ability, "in a narrow way", to block deployment of unsafe technology. He also said an AI pause would only work if all major players, including geopolitical rivals, agreed to it and it could be verified, and that he does not believe China would be a responsible actor.
notes: ABC News interview text read on 6abc. The interview follows a letter Amodei wrote on Wednesday (30 Sep 2026 by the article's wording) and a $200 million research pledge on AI's impact on society; Anthropic's statement about a pause 'last week' is referred to but not quoted. Credit is ABC News; 6abc is the carrier. The ABC News original link was not available.
